reality_delta: Code-level boundary changes appear to have been made (carrier_probe moved before REDCAP_E2E_WORKER, active_run blocking, self-check assertion, project-level .codex/config.toml generation, and a declared blocker for missing Codex CLI project hooks). However, the only evidence available is internal summaries/receipts generated by the same system under review; the prompt-only mode prevents independent verification of diffs, source assertions, or runtime artifacts. The controlled 'negative' run shows the gate blocks, but also shows the probe's OK signal does not correlate with actual project hook lifecycle events, raising questions about what the probe is really measuring.
main_concern: The carrier_probe may be a synthetic/self-referential gate rather than a true probe of Codex CLI hook capability. If the CLI can emit 'carrier-probe-ok' without firing SessionStart/PreToolUse/etc., then the preflight could either falsely pass when hooks are later broken, or the current 'block' is merely documenting an environment gap rather than proving the boundary hardening works against a real hook-capable CLI. The risk of explaining documents/receipts as completion persists.
top_risks: Circular verification: receipts and self-checks are produced by the same runtime being audited; no independent or external evidence is cited.
Probe validity gap: carrier_probe-ok is not shown to imply real project-level hook events, so the gate may not prevent future false positives.
Narrative substitution: accepting 'we documented the hard contract and blocked cleanly' as sufficient could mask that the actual E2E still has no working Hook carrier.
missing_evidence: Independent reproduction of the carrier preflight block with a real Codex CLI version, showing exact stderr/stdout and exit codes outside the project's own receipts.
Source diff or excerpt proving carrier_probe executes before any env["REDCAP_E2E_WORKER"] assignment and that active_run blocking is immutable/auditable downstream.
Confirmation that the patrol loop reads the blocked active_run and stops rather than proceeding to Loom role instantiation or reporting completion.
minimum_fix: Do not claim production readiness. Obtain or build a Codex CLI configuration/invocation that genuinely emits project-level hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop), then re-run the carrier preflight end-to-end. Until then, keep the status as 'boundary scaffolding in place, full E2E blocked by missing hook carrier', and store the blocker in a machine-readable registry the patrol loop consumes.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Previous Prism concern about Codex CLI Hook carrying was upgraded to a declared blocker; however, the 'proof' of blocking is itself another receipt. Need an external signal (real CLI hook trace) before the loop can advance.

user_intent_alignment: Partially aligned. The user explicitly asked not to claim full revival completion and to trigger Prism review. The main AI has refrained from that claim and produced a Prism packet. Misalignment risk: if the user intended a hardened boundary that is also validated against real Hook behavior, the current evidence only shows a self-certified gate and a known-unhookable CLI, which is not the same as a fixed runtime entry.
